n: Paul turns to a shocking report: a member was living in a sexual relationship with his stepmother — something even the pagan world considered scandalous.
Instead of grieving and removing the man from fellowship, the congregation was proud — perhaps of their supposed tolerance.
Though Paul is far away, he is with them in spirit and has already reached a judgment about the man.

f.w: absent in body, but present in spirit

n: He instructs them to act formally, gathered in Christ’s name and with His authority, with Paul united with them in spirit.

f.w: In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ

n: The man is to be excommunicated — handed over to Satan’s territory outside the Church — so that his sinful nature may be broken and his spirit ultimately saved. Church discipline aims at redemption.

f.w: deliver such an one unto Satan
f.g: Expel him from the Church’s protection and fellowship.

f.w: that the spirit may be saved

n: Their boasting is wrong. Just as a pinch of yeast spreads through a whole batch of dough, tolerated sin spreads through a whole community.

f.w: a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump

f.g: Yeast or sourdough starter; often a symbol of corruption.

n: At Passover, Jews cleared every bit of yeast from their homes. Christ is our Passover Lamb, already sacrificed, so the saints should clear sin from their lives.
So let us celebrate the true feast — not with old sin, malice, and wickedness, but with the pure bread of sincerity and truth.
Paul mentions an earlier letter (now lost) in which he told them not to associate with sexually immoral people.

f.g: A previous letter to Corinth that has not survived.

n: He didn’t mean to avoid all immoral or greedy people outside the Church — that would require leaving the world entirely.

f.g: Swindlers, people who take by force or fraud.

n: He meant they shouldn’t keep close fellowship with a professing member who persists in serious sin — not even sharing a meal that signals full approval.

f.g: A verbal abuser, someone who insults and slanders.
Someone claiming to be a Church member.

n: Church discipline isn’t for outsiders. Paul’s and the Church’s responsibility is to judge within the community of members.
God will judge outsiders. The Corinthians must remove the unrepentant sinner from among them, echoing a phrase from Deuteronomy.

f.w: put away from among yourselves that wicked person
